lines.japanese: 「行ってきまーす」
lines.english: “I'm off.”

lines.japanese: 誰に言うわけでもないのに、何故か習慣づいてる出かけの言葉。こういう言葉に返事はいらないのかもしれない。
lines.english: Words I had somehow made a habit of saying whenever I left, though I addressed them to no one in particular. Perhaps words like these needed no reply.

lines.japanese: 口から声を出すことは自らの士気への鼓舞であって、それだけで一日を過ごす活力が沸いてきたり、そこまでいかなくても、とりあえず足だけは進められたり、そんなもの。
lines.english: Saying it out loud was a way to cheer myself on. Sometimes that alone gave me enough energy to get through the day, and even when it didn't, it at least got my feet moving. That was how it worked.

lines.japanese: だから声をかける対象がそこに在ろうと在るまいと、そんなことは僕にとって大きな問題じゃないんだ。
lines.english: So whether anyone was actually there for me to talk to or not wasn't a big deal.

lines.japanese: 朝から散歩なんかしている有閑なお年寄りと、通りすぎざまに挨拶を交わす。
lines.english: I exchanged greetings in passing with elderly people leisurely enough to take a morning stroll.

lines.japanese: 彼らが天気の話題ひとつで見知らぬ誰とでも笑いあえるのは、必ずしも伝えたい意思や情報があるわけじゃないからだろう。
lines.english: Maybe they could laugh about the weather with any stranger because they didn't necessarily have anything they actually wanted or needed to say.

lines.japanese: 声をかけ、声をかけられる。ただ「声」であればいいんだ、意志や情報を伝える「話」である必要はない。だから心に浮かんだよしなしごとをただ口にするだけ。つれづれなるまゝに。僕もそうありたいと願う。
lines.english: To call out and be answered: it only had to be a voice, not talk meant to convey intention or information. You could simply say whatever idle thoughts came to mind, as the spirit moved you. I wished I could be that way too.

lines.japanese: 緩やかな傾斜の先にクラスメイトの家が見えてきた。
lines.english: My classmate's house appeared beyond the gentle slope.

lines.japanese: けれど山科さんの姿は見えない。もしかしたら今日は学校へ行く支度をしてるのだろうか。
lines.english: There was no sign of Yamashina. Perhaps today she was preparing to go to school.

lines.japanese: もし教室で会えたら僕は天気の話をしよう。
lines.english: If I saw her in the classroom, I would talk about the weather.

lines.japanese: 「各駅停車・柳木原行き、ドア閉まりまーす」
lines.english: “Local service for Yanagihara. The doors are now closing.”

lines.japanese: 電車の中で見かける顔にも、いくつか顔見知りみたいな人はいる。
lines.english: A few of the faces I saw on the train were kind of familiar.

lines.japanese: ドアのそばで片耳イヤホンからラジオを聞いてるおじさん。座席の端でコンパクト片手にメイクを施すお姉さん。いつも同じポールに体を預けている、可愛らしい感じの下級生。
lines.english: The older man by the door, listening to the radio through one earbud. The woman at the end of the bench, applying makeup with compact in hand. The cute underclassman who always leaned against the same pole.

lines.japanese: 向こうから見たらどうなんだろう。僕はこれと言って特徴のない顔をしているから、この時間、この車両の常連の中でも知られてない方かもしれない。こんなところでもその他大勢。男子学生Ａだ。
lines.english: I wondered what it was like from their side. I didn't have any features that stood out, so maybe even the regulars in this car at this hour didn't really know my face. Just one of the crowd here too. Male Student A.

lines.japanese: もっとも僕だって、彼らのここでの顔は知っているけど、街中で同じひとを見ても分からないんだと思う。
lines.english: Then again, I knew what they looked like here, but I probably wouldn't recognize the same people if I saw them around town.

lines.japanese: 窓の外の景色をぼうっと眺めた。四角い枠の中に、いくつもの家が並んで、右から左へ消えていく。
lines.english: I gazed blankly through the window. Within its rectangular frame, rows of houses slipped away from right to left.

lines.japanese: この家の数だけ生活があって、それだけの人が僕と同じように、朝起きて目をこすって出かけて行くのかと思うと、不思議な感じだった。
lines.english: Every one of these houses had a life inside it, and all those people got up in the morning, rubbed their eyes, and headed out just like me. It felt strange to think about.

lines.japanese: この屋根だらけの風景の中で、渡来さんも誰かに行ってきますなんて眠そうに言ってるのかな。そんなことが頭に浮かんだ。
lines.english: Among all these rooftops, was Watarai sleepily telling someone she was off too? The thought popped into my head.

lines.japanese: あれ。
lines.english: Wait.

lines.japanese: 教室に入ってまず目に付いたのは、椅子の上で億劫そうに体を反らせる針生さんだった。
lines.english: The first person I noticed when I entered the classroom was Hariu, leaning back in his chair like he couldn't be bothered to move.

lines.japanese: 今日は朝から来てるんだ。本来は当たり前のことなんだけど、彼に限っては珍しい。
lines.english: He was here from the start of the day. That should be normal, but for him it was unusual.

lines.japanese: どうしよう、昨日は少し会話もしたし、今日も挨拶してみようかな。
lines.english: What should I do? We had talked a little yesterday. Maybe I should try greeting him again today.

lines.japanese: そうだ、当たって砕けろだ。もう何度か砕けてるんだから今さらだ。
lines.english: Yes. Go for it and crash and burn. I had already crashed and burned several times; what was one more?

lines.japanese: 「おはようございます」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは頭を揺らしただけで、それ以外に動きは見せなかった。僕はもう一度頭を下げて通りすぎる。
lines.english: Hariu merely rocked his head. Nothing else moved. I bowed once more and went past.

lines.japanese: やっぱり砕けてしまった。でも砕けたくらいじゃ死なないものだ。だから僕は満足することにした。朝は声が出せればそれだけで気持ちがすっきりする。
lines.english: So I crashed and burned after all. But crashing and burning wasn't enough to kill me. I decided that was good enough. Just getting my voice out in the morning made me feel better.

lines.japanese: 「おはよー」
lines.english: “Morning.”

lines.japanese: と思ったら、予期せぬ場所から挨拶が飛んできた。
lines.english: Or so I thought, when a greeting came flying from an unexpected quarter.

lines.japanese: しばらくそのまま固まっていると、片手を上げた渡来さんが、にこやかな表情はそのままに眉だけを八の字に歪ませた。
lines.english: I stayed frozen like that for a while. Watarai kept one hand raised and her smile in place, but her eyebrows twisted into a worried frown.

lines.japanese: 「あれ。私、針生先輩以下？」
lines.english: “Oh. I'm below Hariu?”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「だって。先輩には自分から挨拶したのに、私は無視された」
lines.english: “You went out of your way to greet him, but ignored me when I greeted you.”

lines.japanese: 「挨拶したのに返されないことほど悲しいものはないよね。ふう」
lines.english: “There’s nothing sadder than greeting someone and getting nothing back. Sigh.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないよ。挨拶するのって一方通行でも気持ちいいよ」
lines.english: “That’s not true. A greeting feels good even if it only goes one way.”

lines.japanese: 「自己完結型なんだ。分かるけど、無視されると恥ずかしいから、私はとりあえず返事してもらった方が無難かな」
lines.english: “So you’re the self-contained type. I get it, but being ignored is embarrassing. I’d say getting an answer is the safer bet.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。じゃあ、おはよう渡来さん」
lines.english: “I see. Good morning, then, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん……なんか義務的……」
lines.english: “Hmm... That sounded kind of obligatory...”

lines.japanese: 「おれも挨拶にダメ出しされるとは思わなかったよ」
lines.english: “I never thought my hello would get marked wrong too.”

lines.japanese: 「明日にチャレンジ」
lines.english: “Try again tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは眉間に皺を寄せたまま去っていった──
lines.english: Watarai walked away with her brow still furrowed—

lines.japanese: ──あ、いや、振りかえった。
lines.english: —no. She turned back.

lines.japanese: 「覚えておきなさい」
lines.english: “Remember that.”

lines.japanese: そして優雅な身振りを加えながら自席に戻っていった。よく分からないけど、面白いひとだ。
lines.english: Then, with an elegant flourish, she returned to her seat. I did not quite understand her, but she was an interesting person.
“Hmph...”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんの声がした気がするけど、まぶたが完全に閉じてしまったので、声をかけることはできなかった。
lines.english: I thought I heard Hariu’s voice. But his eyes had closed completely, so I could not speak to him.

lines.japanese: 自分の席へ着いた。鞄を脇にかける。明日は針生さんに挨拶が出来るといいなあ。渡来さんには僕から声をかけられるようにしよう。
lines.english: I sat down at my desk and hung my bag at the side. Maybe tomorrow I'd manage to say hello to Hariu. And with Watarai, I'd try to be the one who spoke first.

lines.japanese: あれ？　そういえば、今まで渡来さんから挨拶してきてくれたことってあったっけ？
lines.english: Wait. Come to think of it, had Watarai ever greeted me first before today?

lines.japanese: なんてことを考えてたら恩田先生がやって来たので、すぐに頭の中を切りかえた。
lines.english: While I was thinking about it, Ms. Onda arrived, and I promptly put it out of my mind.

lines.japanese: 僕はいつもより熱を込めて朝の号令をかけた。
lines.english: I led the morning greeting with more feeling than usual.

lines.japanese: 一限目後の休憩時間。
lines.english: The break after first period.

lines.japanese: 山科さんは来ていなかった。病気のせいで調子が悪いのかな、なんてことを一人で考えた。彼女は今日も出かけようとして波がきたのかもしれない。
lines.english: Yamashina had not come. Maybe her illness had left her feeling unwell, I thought. Perhaps another wave had struck just as she tried to leave the house that morning.

lines.japanese: 薬を処方されてるくらいだからお医者さんにもかかってるんだろうし、僕に出来ることなんてないのかもしれない。
lines.english: If she had been prescribed medicine, she must already be seeing a doctor. There might be nothing I could do for her.

lines.japanese: 今日の帰りにも寄ってみようかな。僕はケータイから繋いだネットで、話の種になりそうな話題をいくつかピックアップしておいた。
lines.english: Maybe I would stop by again on the way home. I went online with my phone and picked out a few subjects that might give us something to talk about.

lines.japanese: そうだ、学校のことを話したら喜んでくれるかな。そう思ってなんとなく教室を見まわしてみる。
lines.english: Maybe hearing about school would make her happy. With that thought, I found myself looking around the classroom.

lines.japanese: 「あれ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんと目が合った……気がした。でも、気のせいかもしれない。
lines.english: My eyes met Hariu’s... or at least I thought they did. Maybe it was my imagination.

lines.japanese: 彼の視線は相変わらずふらふらと泳いで、特定の位置に定まらない。だから僕を見ていたってわけじゃないと思う。
lines.english: His gaze wandered as restlessly as ever, never settling anywhere. I doubted he had really been looking at me.

lines.japanese: だって彼がわざわざ僕に視線を向ける理由が思いつかない。
lines.english: Why would he go out of his way to look at me?

lines.japanese: そう思って、すぐに体を正面に向けた。
lines.english: Thinking that, I immediately faced front again.

lines.japanese: そこには何の変哲もない賑やかな情景があった。
lines.english: Everything looked lively and perfectly ordinary.
